links.outcome: Significant race- or sex-related differences in LLM diagnostic accuracy under counterfactual demographic prompts
links.effect: Ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed across models and conditions; Black patients most often had significantly lower accuracy (4/10 race comparisons).
links.quote: Across models and conditions, ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed.

links.outcome: Effect of prompting strategies on demographic bias and diagnostic accuracy
links.effect: No significant accuracy differences across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 text-only, 0.95 vision); basic and self-consistency gave ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, chain-of-thought none.
links.quote: Text-only and vision models showed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 and 0.95, respectively); basic and self-consistency prompting produced ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, respectively, whereas no significant differences were observed with chain-of-thought prompting.

links.outcome: Subgroup diagnostic accuracy differences by race and sex across LLMs
links.effect: Black patients had significantly lower accuracy in 4 of 10 significant race-related comparisons; vision models with female patients under basic prompting showed 6/10 significant race-related differences.
links.quote: Vision models with female patients under basic prompting showed a higher number of significant race-related differences (6/10 [60%]) than vision models with male patients and all text-only models.
